stable_tendencies: TARGET_A04 can devise unconventional plans independently, sustain secrecy under scrutiny, and exceed others’ expectations on complex logistical tasks. [D1-Q1-C01]
TARGET_A04 tends to refuse dangerous demands through hesitation, ambiguity, omission, or limited noncompliance rather than direct confrontation. [D6-Q2-C02]
TARGET_A04 can conceal or compartmentalize fear and private concerns, making internal distress difficult to infer from outward behavior. [D5-Q2-C01]
TARGET_A04’s conduct appears more responsive to severe, unavoidable consequences than to the passage of time alone. [D5-Q3-C02; D7-Q1-C01]
motives_and_goals: Maintaining parental approval and avoiding rejection or disownment appear to be strong constraints, especially when ordinary punishment would have little effect. [D2-Q2-C02; D8-Q2-C02]
Family attachment is a major channel of motivation and pressure; threats to family safety altered later choices. [D6-Q2-C04; D7-Q1-C02]
TARGET_A04 appears motivated to preserve and publicly reinforce a high-status identity through distinctions, presentation, and prestigious associations. [D7-Q2-C01; D7-Q2-C03]
value_priorities: TARGET_A04 gives substantial weight to family connection, approval, and security. [D2-Q2-C02; D6-Q2-C04]
Earlier evaluations of worth appear organized around inherited standing, wealth, social background, and perceived talent. [D4-Q3-C01]
Later conduct shows increased harm awareness and reduced harmfulness, but not a complete displacement of self-interest or inherited attitudes. [D7-Q3-C03]
cognitive_appraisal_model: TARGET_A04 appears to interpret inherited advantages and perceived talent as grounds for respect and elevated standing. [D4-Q3-C01]
TARGET_A04 tends to regard valued positions as deserved even when outside assistance contributed to obtaining them. [D3-Q1-C03; D7-Q2-C02]
An ideal environment is imagined as one that validates TARGET_A04’s preferred status and places TARGET_A04 above peers rather than challenging that self-image. [D4-Q3-C02]
Challenges to earned status expose tension between feeling deserving and benefiting from improper assistance. [D7-Q3-C02]
When the preferred self-image is threatened, TARGET_A04 may defend it through boasting, unsupported claims, or dismissal of disconfirming evidence. [D7-Q2-C04]
affective_dynamics: Threats against TARGET_A04’s family produce fear and constrain behavior, although they do not guarantee unquestioning obedience. [D8-Q1-C03]
Private fear may be compartmentalized, creating an emotionally opaque exterior. [D5-Q2-C01]
Severe consequences are associated with later guilt, greater awareness of harm, and behavioral moderation. [D7-Q1-C01]
Self-image threats may elicit defensive self-presentation rather than open acknowledgment of compromised merit. [D7-Q2-C04; D7-Q3-C02]
interpersonal_patterns: TARGET_A04 uses ridicule and provocative humor to elicit reactions from disliked peers. [D8-Q3-C02]
Early interpersonal conduct reflects adoption of family-taught prejudice and bullying rather than independent scrutiny of those norms. [D7-Q3-C01]
Care or restraint, when present under coercion, is more likely to be expressed through withheld cooperation than explicit allegiance or open defense. [D6-Q2-C02]
TARGET_A04’s later departures from inherited conduct remain selective and indirect rather than constituting a complete rejection of family influence. [D7-Q1-C03; D7-Q3-C03]
self_narrative_themes: TARGET_A04 appears to maintain a self-image of natural entitlement to elite status and admiration based on talent, wealth, family background, and inherited standing. [D7-Q2-C01]
Early identity is portrayed as closely modeled on family beliefs and expectations. [D7-Q3-C01]
The collapse of an expected high-status life and exposure to severe consequences forced partial revision of inherited conduct. [D7-Q1-C01; D7-Q1-C03]
The resulting change narrative is incomplete: increased awareness and restraint coexist with guilt, self-interest, and remnants of prior attitudes. [D7-Q3-C03]
situation_behavior_signatures: When assigned a difficult operation with room for private planning, TARGET_A04 develops original logistics, conceals the method, and makes substantial progress. [D1-Q1-C01]
When a coercive demand would expose others to grave harm, TARGET_A04 tends toward uncertain answers, omission, delay, or limited noncompliance rather than open resistance. [D6-Q2-C02]
When family members are threatened, TARGET_A04 becomes strongly constrained by fear but may still retain limited independent choice. [D8-Q1-C03]
When harsh consequences become unavoidable, TARGET_A04 is more likely to reduce harmful behavior and revise course. [D5-Q3-C02; D7-Q1-C01]
When status or merit is challenged, TARGET_A04 may protect the preferred identity through boastful or unsupported claims. [D7-Q2-C04]
expressive_signature: TARGET_A04 uses conspicuous presentation, boasting, visible displays, and prestigious associations to signal elevated status. [D7-Q2-C03]
Ridicule is used deliberately as a reaction-seeking social performance against disliked peers. [D8-Q3-C02]
The outward high-status display may function defensively when TARGET_A04’s merit or entitlement is questioned. [D7-Q2-C04]
contradictions_boundary_conditions: Strategic competence and secrecy coexist with later hesitation under morally or emotionally consequential pressure; planning ability does not establish willingness to complete every final act. [D1-Q1-C01; D6-Q2-C02]
Strong family pressure constrains TARGET_A04 but does not eliminate all agency or guarantee obedience. [D6-Q2-C04; D8-Q1-C03]
Earlier prejudice, bullying, and entitlement coexist with later harm reduction; the evidence supports partial revision rather than complete moral transformation. [D7-Q3-C01; D7-Q3-C03]
Emotional concealment is not evidence of emotional absence; outward composure may reveal little about underlying fear. [D5-Q2-C01]
Indirect resistance is context-bound and should not be generalized into readiness for open rebellion or self-sacrifice. [D6-Q2-C02]
unknown_contested: Whether TARGET_A04 would complete a personally lethal act is disputed: substantial enabling behavior and one contrary interpretation coexist with repeated reports of hesitation or stopping short. [D1-Q1-C02; D3-Q3-C01]
Whether avoiding another person’s death is a firm moral boundary, situational aversion, guilt, or self-preservation cannot be resolved from the evidence. [D2-Q3-C01; D3-Q2-C04; D6-Q2-C05]
The relative importance of parental approval, family safety, personal survival, and status under extreme pressure remains disputed. [D1-Q3-C02; D2-Q1-C02; D2-Q2-C01; D5-Q1-C01; D5-Q1-C02]

Whether TARGET_A04 would accept severe violence to preserve family or peer approval is contested by evidence of indirect resistance and reluctance to enable lethal harm. [D2-Q3-C02; D3-Q1-C01; D3-Q1-C02]
Whether later restraint reflects care for former adversaries, moral growth, fear, guilt, or strategic self-protection is uncertain. [D3-Q2-C02; D3-Q2-C04; D6-Q2-C01]
The proposed contrast between friendliness toward an unfamiliar famous peer and concealment around familiar adversaries may reflect danger rather than familiarity. [D1-Q2-C01]
Risk-taking based on overconfidence in controlling dangerous animals is weakly supported and may not generalize beyond the reported setting. [D1-Q3-C01]
High performance expectations and family criticism are weakly evidenced and cannot establish a broad developmental pattern. [D1-Q1-C03]
Avoidance of family or peer rejection as the reason for accompanying others into conflict is based on limited interpretation. [D2-Q2-C03; D6-Q1-C01]
A broad tendency to dominate lower-status peers, use resources or intimidation for compliance, or prioritize entitlement over reciprocity remains weak or contested. [D4-Q3-C04; D6-Q3-C01; D6-Q3-C03]
Strategic cultivation of powerful figures and special attentiveness toward high-status strangers are weakly supported. [D4-Q2-C07; D6-Q1-C05]
Whether TARGET_A04 idealizes untested alternatives because they seem more validating is weakly supported. [D4-Q3-C03]

The intensity and expression of distress are unclear: compartmentalization is supported, while visible crying and an unconvincing cool exterior are disputed or portrayal-dependent. [D5-Q2-C01; D5-Q2-C02; D5-Q3-C06]
Guilt, self-loathing, suppression of shame-linked memories, and hesitation at a critical moment have limited or indirect support. [D5-Q3-C03; D5-Q3-C04; D5-Q3-C05]
Whether harsh punishment merely suppresses bullying or changes underlying views is contested. [D8-Q2-C03]
A consistently loud speaking style, unreliable speech, and highly elaborate performative mockery are weak or disputed expressive claims. [D8-Q3-C01; D8-Q3-C03; D8-Q3-C05]
Selective insults outside authority figures’ hearing and conflict that remains verbal rather than physical are weakly supported and context-specific. [D8-Q3-C04; D6-Q2-C03]
